# Research: Codex as a first-class runtime

**Spec**: [spec.md](spec.md) · **Plan**: [plan.md](plan.md) · **Tasks**: [tasks.md](tasks.md)

Everything below marked Measured was run on `claude-server` on 10/6/26 against
`codex-cli 0.153.4` (`/home/nctiggy/sf-cli/bin/codex`) and tmux 3.4, in a private tmux
server (`tmux -L <name>`) with an isolated `CODEX_HOME`, so the operator's
`~/.codex/config.toml` was not touched. Anything not measured says so.

## M. Measurements

| # | Question | Measured answer |
|---|---|---|
| M1 | What does tmux report as `#{pane_current_command}` while Codex runs? | `node`. `~/sf-cli/bin/codex` is a symlink to `@openai/codex/bin/codex.js`, a Node wrapper that spawns the native binary `…/codex-linux-x64/vendor/x86_64-unknown-linux-musl/bin/codex`. After Codex exits the pane reports `bash`. |
| M2 | Does a pre-written `[projects."<dir>"] trust_level = "trusted"` in `$CODEX_HOME/config.toml` suppress the trust prompt? | Yes. With the table written before start, Codex went straight to the composer. |
| M3 | Does crswd's prompt delivery (`load-buffer`, `paste-buffer -d`, then `send-keys Enter`) submit on Codex? | **No.** The text lands in the composer and the Enter is swallowed. A second Enter sent ~12 s later submitted it. |
| M4 | Does bracketed paste (`paste-buffer -p -d`) followed by `send-keys Enter` submit? | **Yes**, for one line and for a two-line paste. Both turns completed. |
| M5 | Does `/compact` delivered as bracketed paste + Enter work? | Yes. The pane printed `• Context compacted`. |
| M6 | Where is the conversation id before and after the first prompt? | No rollout file exists until the first prompt. After it, the native `codex` process holds the rollout **open**: `/proc/<native pid>/fd/37 -> $CODEX_HOME/sessions/2026/10/06/rollout-2026-10-06T00-11-13-01a10e8c-d5f5-7452-8561-233103b38287.jsonl`, still open while idle after the turn. |
| M7 | Process tree under the pane | `pane_pid` (bash) → `node …/bin/codex` → native `codex`. `/proc/<pid>/task/<pid>/children` lists children on this kernel. |
| M8 | What does Ctrl-C do? | Idle with an empty composer: one `C-c` exits to the shell and prints `To continue this session, run: codex resume <id>`. During a turn: `C-c C-c` interrupts (`■ Conversation interrupted …`) and **does not exit**. Esc then `C-c C-c` one second later also did not exit. |
| M9 | Does a stepped quit converge? | Yes. During a turn with half-typed text in the composer: `C-c`, wait 1.5 s, check `pane_current_command`; repeated, the pane was back at `bash` after the **third** press. |
| M10 | Does `codex resume <id> <flags…>` accept the top-level flags after the subcommand? | Yes. `codex resume <id> --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox --no-alt-screen --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust -c check_for_update_on_startup=false` restored the conversation (history visible, `Context compacted` line included). |
| M11 | `codex resume <id that does not exist>` | Prints `ERROR: No saved session found with ID <id>. Run codex resume without an ID to choose from existing sessions.` and exits to the shell. **No picker.** |
| M12 | Is the update prompt dangerous? | **Yes. This is the most important finding.** On `codex resume`, Codex 0.153.4 drew a blocking menu: `✨ Update available! 0.153.4 -> 0.160.1` / `› 1. Update now (runs npm install -g @openai/codex)` / `2. Skip` / `3. Skip until next version` / `Press enter to continue`. A prompt delivered blind (paste + Enter) selected item 1 and started a global `npm install -g @openai/codex`. It was interrupted by the next Ctrl-C; npm rolled back (verified: `codex --version` still 0.153.4, files still dated 9/8). |
| M13 | Can the update check be turned off per launch? | Yes. `-c check_for_update_on_startup=false` on the command line suppressed the menu on the same `resume` that showed it before. The key is in the binary's config schema. |
| M14 | `codex login status` exit codes | Signed in: prints `Logged in using ChatGPT`, exit 0. Empty `CODEX_HOME`: prints `Not logged in` on **stderr** (stdout is empty), exit 1. Read both streams. |
| M15 | `codex login --device-auth` screen (CLI, not the TUI) | Captured below (§F2). The code is two upper-case alphanumeric groups joined by `-`. |
| M16 | `session_meta` first line of a rollout | JSON object `{"timestamp","ordinal","type":"session_meta","payload":{…}}`; payload keys include `id`, `session_id`, `cwd`, `originator` (`codex-tui`), `cli_version`, `timestamp`, `base_instructions`. Line length on this host: 18–23 KB (62 rollouts, max 22,455 bytes) because `base_instructions` is inline. |
| M17 | tmux regex format match | `#{m/r:^(#{@crswd-binary})$,#{pane_current_command}}` with `@crswd-binary` = `codex\|node\|sleep` (raw bytes `codex|node|sleep`; the backslashes are table escaping) returned `1` for a pane running `sleep`, and `0` with `codex\|node`. tmux 3.4 here; the session image ships 3.5a. |
| M18 | quota-axi `codex` provider | `providers/codex.js:134` names the windows `five_hour` and `weekly`. The cache file on this host (`~/.cache/quota-axi/quotas.json`) holds only the `claude` provider. `quota-axi --provider codex --full` reports `auth_required` although `codex login status` says signed in; this account is Business with unlimited credits, and `account/rateLimits/read` returns `primary: null, secondary: null`. Cause of `auth_required`: **not measured**. |
| M19 | Why does quota-axi report `auth_required` for Codex? | Measured 2026-10-06 by the operator session (quota-axi as installed, Codex 0.153.4). `quota-axi auth` lists `~/.codex/auth.json` and the cli-rpc binary as `available`; the access token is valid (not expired). `quota-axi --provider codex --full`: oauth `failed` "Codex sign-in required", cli-rpc `failed` "Codex quota unavailable". Replaying quota-axi's own oauth request (status codes only): `GET chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/usage` answers **200** with `plan_type: business`, `rate_limit: null`, `credits.unlimited: true`; `GET .../codex/usage` answers **403** (HTML). `normalizeCodexUsage` returns `undefined` when no window exists, so `fetchOauthUsage` treats the 200 as unusable, moves on, meets the 403 and throws "Codex sign-in required". Cause: an unlimited Business account has no windows and quota-axi mislabels that as `auth_required`. **Fix belongs to quota-axi** (report `unlimited`/no-windows from a 200 with `credits.unlimited`). No crswd change: the Codex meter stays hidden while no window exists (NC-1). |

## D. Decisions

Each decision names the rejected alternative and why.

**D1. A harness is derived from the configured command, never stored.**
`harness.Of(command)` is the base name of the command's first token (`startBinary`'s rule,
`internal/session/conversation.go:362`): `claude` → Claude, `codex` → Codex, anything else →
Other. A session already persists its start-command *name* in `@crswd-start` and the journal's
`start` field, and adoption restores both; the harness is recomputed from the configured
command each time it is needed.
*Rejected: a stored `@crswd-runtime` option.* Spec 009's lesson is that a fact tmux does not
hold is lost on adoption. Storing a second copy of something derivable creates a fact that can
disagree with the configuration it came from. *Rejected: a `harness=` field in the
configuration.* It would let an operator label `claude` as Codex; the binary already says what it is.

**D2. A create still carries a name, never a command line.** The operator configures Codex as
a named entry in `start_commands`, e.g.
`codex=/home/nctiggy/sf-cli/bin/codex --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust`.
The browser offers Codex only when an entry named exactly `codex` exists and `harness.Of` of its
command is Codex. The signed API can already name `codex` (`start_command`).
*Rejected: offering every configured name.* That is spec 011's "harness picker" in general form;
this spec ships the two runtimes Craig asked for and keeps the browser's allowlist two entries long.

**D3. Mode (local/remote) stays Claude-only.** `ModeRemote` means `claude --remote-control`.
A Codex session is always `local`; the browser refuses `remote_control=on` with `harness=codex`.
*Rejected: generalising Mode into "which named command".* docs/harnesses.md asked; the answer is
that Mode and harness are different axes, and Codex has no remote mode to put on the second value.

**D4. Remote control for Codex is a non-goal.** `codex remote-control` manages an app-server
daemon that the ChatGPT mobile app pairs with; it does not attach to a TUI running in tmux
(research-codex.md §1). Spec 018's typed input is how a Codex session is driven from a phone.

**D5. Required flags are added by the daemon, not left to configuration.** Codex's harness spec
carries two flag groups that crswd inserts after the binary on every line it types, unless the
exact token sequence is already in the configured command:
- `--no-alt-screen`: without it Codex draws on the alternate screen and tmux keeps no history,
  which defeats spec 018's scrollback.
- `-c check_for_update_on_startup=false`: M12. Without it any typed input can install software.
The approval/sandbox and hook-trust flags stay the operator's choice, as
`--dangerously-skip-permissions` is for Claude. *Rejected: documenting the two flags and trusting
the operator.* M12 shows a forgotten flag costs a global package install; a daemon that types into
the pane has to own the flags that make typing safe.

**D6. Liveness compares against a set of names.** `@crswd-binary` changes from one name to names
joined by `|` (each still `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`), and the tmux format becomes
`#{?#{@crswd-binary},#{m/r:^(#{@crswd-binary})$,#{pane_current_command}},?}` (M17). Codex writes
`codex|node`; every other harness writes `startBinary(template)` exactly as today, so a Claude
session's option value and liveness answer are unchanged.
*Rejected: walking `/proc` from the daemon on every sweep.* One tmux format is cheaper and is what
podctl already reuses through `tmuxctl.ArgvList`. *Rejected: requiring the operator to configure
the native binary path.* The npm path is what is installed; a session that reads as permanently
stopped would be revived in a loop.
*Accepted risk:* while Codex runs, any `node` in the pane foreground reads as alive. The pane runs
nothing but the configured command.

**D7. Codex conversations are discovered from `/proc`, not guessed.** Codex cannot be given an id
(no `--session-id`; `ThreadStartParams` has no id field). M6 shows the native process holds its
rollout open, so on each supervisor sweep a running Codex session with no conversation reads
`#{pane_pid}`, walks its descendants through `/proc/<pid>/task/<pid>/children` (depth ≤ 6, ≤ 64
processes), and reads each `/proc/<pid>/fd/*` link. A link matching
`<codexHome>/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-*-<uuid>.jsonl` yields the id.
*Rejected: matching rollouts by `cwd` and start time.* Two Codex sessions in one directory make it
a guess, and a wrong guess resumes someone else's conversation.
*Before the first prompt there is no id.* The session is supervised but not revivable by id, which
is exactly how a Claude session created before spec 012 behaves (`reasonNoConversation`). The card
says "conversation not yet started".

**D8. Restarting a Codex session uses a stepped, verified quit.** Continue (spec 013) and revival
type a new command line into the pane. Into a live Codex composer that line becomes a prompt. So
for Codex `restartInto` sends one `C-c`, waits 1.5 s, asks tmux whether the pane is still running
the harness (D6), and repeats, at most 5 presses (M9 converged in 3). If the pane is still running
Codex after the fifth, it returns `ErrQuitUnconfirmed` and types nothing. Claude keeps `C-c C-c`.
*Rejected: `/quit` via paste.* While a turn runs, Codex queues typed input, so `/quit` would wait.

**D9. Prompt and compact use bracketed paste on Codex (M3, M4, M5).**
Spec 018 adds `Controller.PasteBracketed` (`paste-buffer -p`). Claude keeps `Paste`; spec 018 owns
whether Claude moves to bracketed paste too.

**D10. Codex trust is seeded by a line-level edit of `config.toml`.** No TOML library: the root
module has no dependencies (docs/security.md §5). The edit understands exactly one shape, the one
Codex itself writes (M2 and research-codex.md §5): a header line `[projects."<dir>"]` and a
`trust_level = "<value>"` line in that table. Anything else that mentions the directory refuses
rather than edits. Same lock file convention and atomic replace as `trust.go` (`<file>.lock`,
temp file, rename). A missing `config.toml` is created at 0600 when `$CODEX_HOME` exists, because
Codex's own trust acceptance creates the same table in the same file; a missing `$CODEX_HOME`
is left missing (Codex has never run, and will show sign-in first).
*Rejected: `-c 'projects."<dir>".trust_level="trusted"'` on the command line.* It puts a
caller-influenced path into a line typed at a shell. No line crswd types has ever carried a path.

**D11. Codex conversation listing opens the first line of a rollout, bounded.** Spec 013 FR-025
says no transcript is opened, because Claude's file name is the id and its directory is the cwd.
Codex keys rollouts by date, and the cwd exists only inside line 1. The reader opens a rollout,
reads at most 64 KiB, stops at the first newline, and decodes only `type`, `payload.id` and
`payload.cwd`. Nothing it reads is rendered. It scans at most 500 rollout files, newest date
directory first, and returns at most 50 matches. docs/security.md records this amendment.

**D12. Sign-in for Codex is a device-code relay with no paste-back.** `codex login --device-auth`
prints a link and a code (F2); the operator enters the code in a browser and the CLI polls. So the
Codex relay shows the link and the code and has no code form; `Deliver` refuses with
`ErrNoCodeToDeliver`. Status comes from `codex login status`'s exit code (M14): 0 signed in;
1 with `Not logged in` on stdout signed out; anything else unknown.
*Rejected: `codex login` (browser).* It opens a localhost callback a phone cannot reach.

**D13. One relay, one auth cache, one pill per harness that is configured.** The single
`Server.signin` becomes a map keyed by `harness.Name`, built for Claude when the default command is
Claude (unchanged) and for Codex when an entry named `codex` exists. `GET /dashboard/auth` keeps
its wire shape and gains `?harness=codex`; absent means Claude, so the existing client is unchanged.
The create gate asks the relay of the harness the create resolves to.

**D14. Codex quota reads the `codex` provider's `weekly` window (M18).** The reader becomes
`ReadProvider(path, provider, window)`. When the cache has no `codex` provider or no window
the Codex meter is hidden (NC-1, Craig 2026-10-06), which is what this host will show today. The quota-axi `auth_required`
cause is investigated by one spike task (T034) and changes no crswd code.

**D15. Kubernetes mode for Codex is gated on spec 017 and on one measurement.** Operator-run
measurement O-1 (tasks.md) measures whether Codex runs a turn with `auth.json` delivered the way spec
017 FR-015 delivers Claude's credential. It needs a cluster and a real credential, so it is not a
loop task. Phase 4's credential tasks are planned from that measurement
in a follow-up planning pass; this spec does not guess them. The tasks that do not depend on it
(env pass-through, the in-pod conversation lookup, the session image) are written here.

#### Detecting death

- **FR-006**: The daemon MUST detect, without operator action, both kinds of
  death: a session whose Claude process has stopped while its shell survives, and
  a session whose shell no longer exists at all.
- **FR-007**: Detection MUST NOT read the content of a session's pane or its
  conversation transcript.
- **FR-008**: Detection MUST run on a recurring sweep whose resolution is finer
  than the delay an operator would notice, and MUST NOT depend on a request
  arriving.

#### Reviving

- **FR-009**: On detecting a dead session that is eligible for revival, the daemon
  MUST restart it so that it continues its recorded conversation.
- **FR-010**: A revived session MUST keep its identity, its owner, its working
  directory, its start command and its absolute deadline. Revival MUST NOT extend
  a session's lifetime or issue it a new deadline.
- **FR-011**: A revived session MUST NOT count as a new session against the
  concurrent-session cap, and revival MUST NOT take the fleet over that cap.
- **FR-012**: Revival MUST NOT run for a session the operator destroyed, for a
  session the reaper destroyed, or for a session past its deadline.

755	// promptSession is POST /sessions/{id}/prompt: deliver the caller's text into
756	// the session it named and say it arrived (contracts/http-api.md).
757	//
758	// The session comes from the context and nowhere else. By the time this runs,
759	// layer 3 has matched the {id} against a record the caller owns and the
760	// credential issued for it, and has stamped that record's ID on the audit
761	// record — so this handler neither reads the path nor sets a session ID, and
762	// there is no version of it that could act on a session it was not given.
763	//
764	// Delivery itself belongs to internal/session, which is the only thing here that
765	// can cause execution on the host. What is left is the HTTP half: read the one
766	// field, hand it over unaltered, and answer.
767	//
768	// The dialog check reads the pane before Prompt runs, deliberately. It asks
769	// what the keystroke is about to land in rather than what the pane holds
770	// afterwards, because the keystroke itself may dismiss or change a menu —
771	// checking after would be asking the question once the answer had moved.
772	func (s *Server) promptSession(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
773		resolved, ok := SessionFrom(r.Context())
774		if !ok {
775			s.failInternal(w, r, errPromptNoSession)
776			return
777		}
778	
779		req, ok := decode[promptRequest](s, w, r)
780		if !ok {
781			return
782		}
783	
784		// Guarded on the same emptiness Manager.Prompt itself refuses on
785		// (ErrEmptyPrompt), so that a body this route was always going to reject
786		// still costs the host nothing at all — not even a read. Duplicating the
787		// bare emptiness check here is not duplicating the rule: Manager.Prompt
788		// still owns ErrEmptyPrompt and every other reason a prompt can be
789		// refused, and refusePrompt below still asks it rather than assuming.
790		var parkedOn string
791		var suspicious bool
792		if req.Text != "" {
793			parkedOn, suspicious = s.paneDialogState(r.Context(), resolved)
794		}
795	
796		if err := s.sessions.Prompt(r.Context(), resolved, req.Text); err != nil {
797			s.refusePrompt(w, r, err)
798			return
799		}
800	
801		// 202, not 200: what is confirmed is that the keystrokes reached the pane,
802		// which is not the same claim as Claude having read them, and the contract
803		// spells that difference as "accepted for delivery". ParkedOn and
804		// SuspiciousDialog narrow that further still: they say the keystrokes
805		// reached a dialog rather than a prompt, when the pane check above found
806		// one to say it about.
807		s.writeJSON(w, r, http.StatusAccepted, promptResponse{
808			ID:               resolved.ID,
809			Delivered:        true,
810			ParkedOn:         parkedOn,
811			SuspiciousDialog: suspicious,
812		})
813	}

816	// sitting on a known TUI dialog (internal/session/dialog.go), for a prompt
817	// about to be delivered into it.
818	//

820	// existed — an ordinary delivery, with neither field set — because a
821	// heuristic's own precondition failing is not a reason to treat an otherwise

826	// read can only ever upgrade the answer, never downgrade one an operator would
827	// otherwise have gotten.
828	func (s *Server) paneDialogState(ctx context.Context, resolved session.Session) (parkedOn string, suspicious bool) {
829		capture, err := s.sessions.Output(ctx, resolved)
830		if err != nil {
831			return "", false
832		}

836		}

841	//

843	// same uniform body every other refused body gets. Everything else is a 500 with

850		if errors.Is(err, session.ErrEmptyPrompt) {
851			s.rejectBadRequest(w, r, session.ErrEmptyPrompt)
852			return
853		}
854		s.failInternal(w, r, errPromptUndelivered)

861	// prompt, and the capture itself belongs to internal/session — the stripper runs
862	// where output leaves that package, so what arrives here is already the bytes
863	// that may go out.
864	//

866	// not be read is a fact about the host: whether tmux is missing, whether the
867	// server died, or whether the window vanished under a record that still resolves
868	// are distinctions an operator reads in the trail, and telling them apart for a
869	// caller would be an oracle about a machine it cannot otherwise see.
870	//
871	// Nothing about the capture reaches the audit record. The middleware's record
872	// says which session was read and by whom, and that is the whole of what FR-042
873	// permits: pane content is secret, and a trail carrying it would be a second,
874	// permanent copy of everything the session ever printed.

input.content:
# Research: prompt route safety

**Spec**: [spec.md](spec.md) · **Plan**: [plan.md](plan.md) · **Tasks**: [tasks.md](tasks.md)

This feature hardens `POST /sessions/{id}/prompt`, the one API route that already
delivers free text into a running session. It is the route ai-lawnmower's `answer`
and opp-lease handoff call today, so every change here is a change to a live client.

## Where the evidence comes from

Three sources, and each decision below says which one it leans on.

| Tag | Source | Status |
|---|---|---|
| **Probe** | `~/code/ai-lawnmower/ralph/plans/lm-steer-design/results.md`, numbered checks | Outside this repo, read-only. The checks this feature turns on are transcribed into `ralph/plans/lm-steer-crswd-018/PROGRESS.md` ("Probe results that decide this plan") because the loop that implements this spec cannot reach that path |
| **Design** | `~/code/ai-lawnmower/docs/mcp-session-steering-design.md`, section (g) "Phase 3 detail" | Outside this repo, read-only. It is where requirements 1 to 7 are stated |
| **Code** | This repository at `30941f3` | Read and re-read in tree on 10/14/26; the line references below were checked, not remembered |

The decisions were taken during planning, before any task ran, and are recorded in
`ralph/plans/lm-steer-crswd-018/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` under "Decisions already
made". They are reproduced here with their evidence. **They are not reopened by the
implementation**; a task that finds one of them wrong stops and says so rather than
choosing differently.

## The route as it stands (Code, 10/14/26)

What the hardening is measured against:

- `internal/httpapi/sessions.go` `promptSession` (line 772) decodes `promptRequest`,
  best-effort-reads the pane for a known dialog (`paneDialogState`, which is
  additive information and never a gate), calls `Manager.Prompt`, and answers `202`
  with `{"id","delivered","parked_on","suspicious_dialog"}`.
- `refusePrompt` (line 849) maps `session.ErrEmptyPrompt` to `400` and **everything
  else to a `500` with no detail**. There is no 409 on this route today.
- `internal/session/manager.go` `Manager.Prompt` (line 1194) refuses an empty ID
  (`ErrSessionNotFound`), `StateDead` (`ErrSessionDead`) and empty text
  (`ErrEmptyPrompt`); takes `lockSession`; calls `m.paste`; then `SendKeys` Enter.
- `m.paste` (line 1253) is bracketed **only** when the harness spec says
  `BracketedPaste`, which Claude's does not (spec 019 D9 left that to spec 018, and
  spec 018 FR-006 declined it for the API door).
- `Manager.Prompt` does **not** read liveness, does **not** consult `StateFailed`,
  and does **not** take the restart claim.

So a prompt into a session whose Claude has exited lands in a login shell as a
command line, and a prompt racing a revival lands half in one process and half in
the next. Those are the two failures this feature closes.

---

## D1 Spec number

**Decision.** This feature is `specs/020-prompt-route-safety/`.

**Evidence.** The design calls it "crswd spec 018", but `specs/018-interactive-input`
(the session page's input panel) and `specs/019-codex-runtime` already exist in this
repository (Code: `ls specs/`). 020 is the first free number.

The milestone directory keeps the design's name — `ralph/plans/lm-steer-crswd-018/` —
because the lawnmower side refers to it that way. The mismatch is deliberate and is
stated in `VALIDATION_CONTRACT.md` so that a later reader does not "fix" one to match
the other.

---

## D2 Liveness gate (requirement 1)

**Decision.** `Manager.Prompt` reads the session's row from the controller's `List`
and branches on its `Claude` liveness:

- `LivenessStopped` → refuse with `ErrSessionNotReady`, before any tmux command that
  changes anything.
- `LivenessUnknown` → deliver.
- `LivenessRunning` → deliver.
- A `List` that fails → an error, not a delivery.

The gate runs **twice**: once before the paste, and again after the paste and before
the Enter. If the second read is stopped, the daemon sends `C-u` and no Enter.

**Evidence.**

- Probe check 13: `@crswd-binary` matched `pane_current_command` on 6 of 6 live panes,
  three of them `rcq` panes. So the option the daemon already sets is a true liveness
  signal for the sessions lawnmower actually drives, not only for the plain case.
- Code: `tmuxctl.SessionInfo.Claude` is the three-valued `Liveness`
  (`internal/tmuxctl/controller.go:312-341`), derived from `@crswd-binary` against the
  pane's current command — by one tmux format in `Exec` (`exec.go:548`) and by
  `livenessOf` in the fake (`fake.go:251`). Both exist already; nothing new is
  measured here.
- Spec 012 FR-006 ("detect a session whose Claude process has stopped while its shell
  survives") is the requirement this reads, and `supervisor.go:153-156` already treats
  `LivenessUnknown` as healthy with a comment saying it must. This gate reads it the
  same way, so a session created before `@crswd-binary` existed keeps working.
- Probe check 1: there is no check-then-Enter race after the first turn; the lost-Enter
  window is the first ~5 s after launch, which is out of scope (D9). That is why two
  reads around the paste are enough and a third is not.

**Why `List` and not a new method.** A per-session liveness method on
`tmuxctl.Controller` would force a matching change in the k8s module's `podctl`
(Code: `k8s/` is a second module reaching the root's `internal/` through `replace ../`).
This milestone adds no `Controller` method, so `podctl` is untouched and the cluster
build does not move.

**Why the second read, and why `C-u`.** Between the paste and the Enter the pane can
fall back to a shell — Claude exits, the composer's text is gone, and the Enter would
submit whatever the paste left on the shell's line as a command. `C-u` clears that
line; sending no Enter means nothing runs. Refusing *after* a paste is not as good as
refusing before one, and the `C-u` is what makes the imperfect case harmless rather
than merely reported.

*Rejected: refusing `LivenessUnknown`.* It is the state of every session started by a
build older than the option, and refusing it would make this route stop working for
sessions the supervisor itself calls healthy — two answers to one question.

*Rejected: reading the pane's text to decide readiness.* Spec 012 FR-007 forbids it
for detection, pane content is secret under `docs/security.md` §3, and `paneDialogState`
already shows what a text read is good for: additive information, never a gate.

---

## D3 Not-ready answer (requirements 1, 2 and 5)

**Decision.** One new sentinel, `session.ErrSessionNotReady`. Every refusal this
feature adds inside `internal/session` returns it, and `refusePrompt` maps it to
`409` with body `{"error":"session not ready"}` and an audit **Deny** whose reason is
the constant `session not ready`.

A session in `StateFailed` gets it. `StateDead` keeps today's answer unchanged.

**Evidence.**

- Code: `StateFailed` (`internal/session/session.go:86`) means the supervisor tried to
  bring the session back and ran out of attempts (`supervisor.go:311-314`). Nothing is
  running in that pane, so a prompt into it is the same failure as a stopped pane;
  `Manager.Prompt` refuses `StateDead` today and says nothing about `StateFailed`.
- Code: a dead session is already refused as a `404` by the resolver before
  `promptSession` runs, and `refusePrompt`'s comment says reaching its `ErrSessionDead`
  branch would mean a record went terminal between two layers of one request. Leaving
  `dead` alone keeps that path exactly as it is and keeps the enumeration rule
  (`docs/security.md`: a session the caller may not have is a 404, never a 403/409).
- lawnmower's `deliver()` (`~/code/ai-lawnmower/loop/session_resume.py`, as recorded in
  PROGRESS.md on 10/14/26) treats **any** body carrying an `error` key as a refusal. So
  `409 {"error":"session not ready"}` reads as a refusal to the existing client with no
  client change, which is why the body carries `error` and not a new key.
- `docs/security.md` "Rate limiting & audit": every reason on the trail is a sentinel
  this codebase authored. `session not ready` is one. It names no state, no pane
  content and no prompt — an operator reading the trail learns that the route refused
  and why in the daemon's own words, and a caller learns nothing about the host it
  could not already see.

*Rejected: a sentinel per reason* (stopped pane, failed state, restart held). Three
sentinels reaching one status code with one body is three things to keep in step for
a distinction the caller cannot observe. The trail distinguishes nothing more here
because the three are the same event to the client: not now, try later.

*Rejected: `503`.* The condition is about one named session, not about this daemon's
capacity, and `409` is already the contract's "the host's state refuses this" code
(the unverified-teardown answer, `sessions.go:749`).

---

## D4 Bracketed paste (requirement 3)

**Decision.** `Manager.Prompt` pastes with `PasteBracketed` for **every** harness.
`Manager.Compact` keeps its harness-based paste (`m.paste`). No newline refusal.

**Evidence.**

- Code: `Controller.PasteBracketed` already exists (spec 018 added it; `paste-buffer -p`,
  `internal/tmuxctl/exec.go:220-230`), and the session page's type route already uses it
  for every harness. This decision reuses that method; it adds none.
- `docs/security.md` §2: inside a bracketed paste the terminal does not interpret the
  pasted bytes, which is what makes multi-line text one paste instead of a line of text
  plus a submit plus another line. The same section already requires that caller text
  reach tmux only through `load-buffer` on stdin and then `paste-buffer`, bracketed on
  the session page's route; this extends the bracketing to the API door's route.
- Spec 019 D9 / research M3–M5 measured that Codex swallows the Enter after a *plain*
  paste and submits correctly after a bracketed one. Claude accepts both. So bracketed
  is the one form that is correct for both harnesses, and `Prompt` stops needing to ask
  which harness it is talking to at all.
- `docs/security.md` §2 also names the one byte that matters inside a bracketed paste:
  text holding a C0 control other than TAB or LF is refused, because `ESC[201~` would
  end the paste. That refusal is spec 018 FR-004's and already runs on the text this
  route accepts.

**Why no newline refusal.** The opp-lease handoff pastes multi-line item bodies
(Probe/Design: the builders in `console.py` and `lawnmower-route`, whose shapes are
fixed byte-for-byte as T011's fixtures in PROGRESS.md "Payload fixtures"). A rule
refusing `\n` would refuse the traffic this route exists to carry. Bracketing is what
makes a newline safe; refusing newlines would be the same protection obtained by
breaking the client.

**Why `Compact` is untouched.** Its payload is a daemon constant, not caller text, and
spec 018 FR-006's "unchanged" promise about this route is amended here only for what
requirements 1 to 6 name. Changing `Compact` as well would be an unrequested change to
a path with no requirement behind it (constitution IV).

This amends spec 018 **FR-006**, which says the API door's prompt route must be
unchanged — plain paste, then Enter, with bracketed paste reserved for the interactive
route. The amendment is recorded in spec.md, not left to this file.

---

## D5 Leading `!` or `/` (requirement 4)

**Decision.** On the **API door only**: refuse a prompt whose first character that is
not space, tab, CR or LF is `!` or `/`. The answer is `400` with the uniform
bad-request body, decided before any tmux command runs. The session page's type route
is unchanged.

**Evidence.**

- Design, requirement 4: those two characters are Claude Code's slash-command and
  shell-escape prefixes. A prompt that begins with one is not a prompt — `/clear`
  discards the conversation the caller was trying to continue, and `!` runs a shell
  command in the session's own unsandboxed context. A client that meant to say
  something and instead silently reset the session is the failure being closed.
- Code grep of 10/14/26 over every lawnmower caller of this route: `console.py`
  `_answer_action` (via `session_resume.deliver`), `lawnmower-route` `resume_prompt`,
  `_batch_listing_prompt`, and `opp_followup_prompt` all build text whose first
  character is a letter. **No existing caller is refused by this rule.** That is the
  whole of why it can be added to a live route at all.
- The fixtures in PROGRESS.md keep the shape that matters: `resume.txt` holds a *later*
  line beginning `/compact`. The rule is about the first non-whitespace character of
  the whole text and nothing else, so that fixture is accepted. A rule scanning every
  line would refuse real traffic.
- The browser door is excluded because its route is the operator typing at their own
  session: `docs/security.md` records the session page's input panel as text or a key
  the operator sent, delivered once, when they pressed it. An operator typing
  `/compact` into their own session is the feature, not a mistake, and T004 asserts
  that it still arrives.

the caller did not write, into a session that executes code. A refusal the client can
see and fix is strictly better than a silent rewrite.

tracks Claude Code's command set, and a stale list is a command delivered because
nobody updated a table. The route carries prompts; a caller that wants a command has
the browser door and the operator behind it.

the interactive route does not have.

**after** `lockSession`, refuses with `ErrSessionNotReady` when a revive or a continue
already holds it, and releases it on return.

  shared by Type, PressKey, Prompt, Compact, SetMode, Continue, Destroy and the
  supervisor's Codex discovery. `Prompt` already takes it (`manager.go:1209`), so two
  concurrent prompts already cannot interleave paste and Enter.

  `exec.go:186-195`, 16 random hex digits behind `BufferPrefix`, "per call rather than
  per session, so a second paste into the same session cannot overwrite the first
  one's text before it lands"). The fake records the names through `nextBuffer`, so a
  test can assert they differ. Both halves of requirement 5's "distinct buffers, no
  interleaving" are therefore **already true**, from the spec 018 and 019 review
  passes, and this feature only has to prove it (T010) rather than build it.

  restart does not hold the session lock for its whole run. A prompt pasted into a pane

  line is about to be typed at.

open across a process restart, and the caller cannot tell a slow delivery from a lost
one. `409 session not ready` is a fact the client can act on now; lawnmower's
`deliver()` already reads it as a refusal (D3).

rule enters the package.

**Decision.** The prompt body gains one optional field, `request_id`: 1 to 32
characters of `[a-z0-9-]`. A value outside that is a `400`. A valid value is echoed in
the `202` body and written as `request_id` on the request's one audit record. Absent
means the field appears nowhere — not in the response, not on the record.

**Evidence.**

- Design, requirement 6: the caller needs to correlate a delivery it made with the
  record of that delivery, across a daemon restart and without a transcript. The audit
  trail is the only durable record of a prompt, and today it carries nothing the caller
  chose.
- Code: `audit.Record` (`internal/audit/audit.go`) has Action, Caller, SessionID,
  Decision, Reason and Remote. `RequestAudit` (`internal/httpapi/middleware.go`) has
  `SetSessionID` and `Deny`, so the carry-it-onto-the-one-record mechanism exists and
  gains one setter (T002) rather than a second record.

  struct with `DisallowUnknownFields`, so the field has to be declared to be accepted
  at all, and anything else in the body is still refused.

operator reads and a tool greps. Lower-case, digits and `-` is the same shape this
repository already holds session names to (`^[a-zA-Z0-9-]{1,64}$`, `docs/security.md`

output, credentials and the shared secret on an audit record, and nothing in it
contemplated a caller-chosen correlation value. This amends FR-042 for **this one
field**, and the bound is exact: the record gains the `request_id` the caller sent and
**nothing about the prompt** — not its text, not its length, not a hash of it. The
alphabet is what keeps the field from becoming a channel for the text itself: 32 bytes
of `[a-z0-9-]` cannot carry a prompt, and a caller that tried would be writing a value
an operator can see is not an identifier. The amendment is recorded in spec.md.

---

## D8 Registry gate (requirement 7) — deferred, not a clarification

**Decision.** Requirement 7, a readiness gate reading Claude Code's session registry,
is **out of scope** for this feature. It is listed under Out of scope in spec.md with
this reason. It is **not** a `NEEDS CLARIFICATION`.

**Evidence.**

- The design states requirement 7 as a **MAY**, not a MUST. Deferring a MAY is a scope
  decision, not an unanswered question, and constitution II is about requirements that
  are *ambiguous* — this one is clear and declined.
- Probe check 8 left open whether crswd can read `sessions/<pid>.json` at all under
  spec 017's v2 option B. No FR in spec 017 places that file in a pod, so a gate built
  on it would work on the VM and silently do nothing in the cluster — a readiness check
  that is right about one deployment and blind in the other.
- Probe checks 3 and 9: the registry misses the trust dialog and misses a half-typed
  draft in the composer. So it answers "a session exists" and not "this session will
  read what I send next", which is the question requirement 7 was asked to answer.

  daemon already holds, and it is what ships.

unchanged by this feature, and spec 019 D11's bounded Codex rollout read stays the
single exception it already is.

**Decision.** This feature does not do any of the following, and a task that finds
itself needing one stops rather than widening:

# Research: prompt route safety

**Spec**: [spec.md](spec.md) · **Plan**: [plan.md](plan.md) · **Tasks**: [tasks.md](tasks.md)

This feature hardens `POST /sessions/{id}/prompt`, the one API route that already
delivers free text into a running session. It is the route ai-lawnmower's `answer`
and opp-lease handoff call today, so every change here is a change to a live client.

## Where the evidence comes from

Three sources, and each decision below says which one it leans on.

| Tag | Source | Status |
|---|---|---|
| **Probe** | `~/code/ai-lawnmower/ralph/plans/lm-steer-design/results.md`, numbered checks | Outside this repo, read-only. The checks this feature turns on are transcribed into `ralph/plans/lm-steer-crswd-018/PROGRESS.md` ("Probe results that decide this plan") because the loop that implements this spec cannot reach that path |
| **Design** | `~/code/ai-lawnmower/docs/mcp-session-steering-design.md`, section (g) "Phase 3 detail" | Outside this repo, read-only. It is where requirements 1 to 7 are stated |
| **Code** | This repository at `30941f3` | Read and re-read in tree on 10/14/26; the line references below were checked, not remembered |

The decisions were taken during planning, before any task ran, and are recorded in
`ralph/plans/lm-steer-crswd-018/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` under "Decisions already
made". They are reproduced here with their evidence. **They are not reopened by the
implementation**; a task that finds one of them wrong stops and says so rather than
choosing differently.

## The route as it stands (Code, 10/14/26)

What the hardening is measured against:

- `internal/httpapi/sessions.go` `promptSession` (line 772) decodes `promptRequest`,
  best-effort-reads the pane for a known dialog (`paneDialogState`, which is
  additive information and never a gate), calls `Manager.Prompt`, and answers `202`
  with `{"id","delivered","parked_on","suspicious_dialog"}`.
- `refusePrompt` (line 849) maps `session.ErrEmptyPrompt` to `400` and **everything
  else to a `500` with no detail**. There is no 409 on this route today.
- `internal/session/manager.go` `Manager.Prompt` (line 1194) refuses an empty ID
  (`ErrSessionNotFound`), `StateDead` (`ErrSessionDead`) and empty text
  (`ErrEmptyPrompt`); takes `lockSession`; calls `m.paste`; then `SendKeys` Enter.
- `m.paste` (line 1253) is bracketed **only** when the harness spec says
  `BracketedPaste`, which Claude's does not (spec 019 D9 left that to spec 018, and
  spec 018 FR-006 declined it for the API door).
- `Manager.Prompt` does **not** read liveness, does **not** consult `StateFailed`,
  and does **not** take the restart claim.

So a prompt into a session whose Claude has exited lands in a login shell as a
command line, and a prompt racing a revival lands half in one process and half in
the next. Those are the two failures this feature closes.

---

## D1 Spec number

**Decision.** This feature is `specs/020-prompt-route-safety/`.

**Evidence.** The design calls it "crswd spec 018", but `specs/018-interactive-input`
(the session page's input panel) and `specs/019-codex-runtime` already exist in this
repository (Code: `ls specs/`). 020 is the first free number.

The milestone directory keeps the design's name — `ralph/plans/lm-steer-crswd-018/` —
because the lawnmower side refers to it that way. The mismatch is deliberate and is
stated in `VALIDATION_CONTRACT.md` so that a later reader does not "fix" one to match
the other.

---

## D2 Liveness gate (requirement 1)

**Decision.** `Manager.Prompt` reads the session's row from the controller's `List`
and branches on its `Claude` liveness:

- `LivenessStopped` → refuse with `ErrSessionNotReady`, before any tmux command that
  changes anything.
- `LivenessUnknown` → deliver.
- `LivenessRunning` → deliver.
- A `List` that fails → an error, not a delivery.

The gate runs **twice**: once before the paste, and again after the paste and before
the Enter. If the second read is stopped, the daemon sends `C-u` and no Enter.

**Evidence.**

- Probe check 13: `@crswd-binary` matched `pane_current_command` on 6 of 6 live panes,
  three of them `rcq` panes. So the option the daemon already sets is a true liveness
  signal for the sessions lawnmower actually drives, not only for the plain case.
- Code: `tmuxctl.SessionInfo.Claude` is the three-valued `Liveness`
  (`internal/tmuxctl/controller.go:312-341`), derived from `@crswd-binary` against the
  pane's current command — by one tmux format in `Exec` (`exec.go:548`) and by
  `livenessOf` in the fake (`fake.go:251`). Both exist already; nothing new is
  measured here.
- Spec 012 FR-006 ("detect a session whose Claude process has stopped while its shell
  survives") is the requirement this reads, and `supervisor.go:153-156` already treats
  `LivenessUnknown` as healthy with a comment saying it must. This gate reads it the
  same way, so a session created before `@crswd-binary` existed keeps working.
- Probe check 1: there is no check-then-Enter race after the first turn; the lost-Enter
  window is the first ~5 s after launch, which is out of scope (D9). That is why two
  reads around the paste are enough and a third is not.

**Why `List` and not a new method.** A per-session liveness method on
`tmuxctl.Controller` would force a matching change in the k8s module's `podctl`
(Code: `k8s/` is a second module reaching the root's `internal/` through `replace ../`).
This milestone adds no `Controller` method, so `podctl` is untouched and the cluster
build does not move.

**Why the second read, and why `C-u`.** Between the paste and the Enter the pane can
fall back to a shell — Claude exits, the composer's text is gone, and the Enter would
submit whatever the paste left on the shell's line as a command. `C-u` clears that
line; sending no Enter means nothing runs. Refusing *after* a paste is not as good as
refusing before one, and the `C-u` is what makes the imperfect case harmless rather
than merely reported.

*Rejected: refusing `LivenessUnknown`.* It is the state of every session started by a
build older than the option, and refusing it would make this route stop working for
sessions the supervisor itself calls healthy — two answers to one question.

*Rejected: reading the pane's text to decide readiness.* Spec 012 FR-007 forbids it
for detection, pane content is secret under `docs/security.md` §3, and `paneDialogState`

---

**Decision.** One new sentinel, `session.ErrSessionNotReady`. Every refusal this
feature adds inside `internal/session` returns it, and `refusePrompt` maps it to
`409` with body `{"error":"session not ready"}` and an audit **Deny** whose reason is
the constant `session not ready`.

**Evidence.**

- Code: `StateFailed` (`internal/session/session.go:86`) means the supervisor tried to
  bring the session back and ran out of attempts (`supervisor.go:311-314`). Nothing is
  running in that pane, so a prompt into it is the same failure as a stopped pane;
  `Manager.Prompt` refuses `StateDead` today and says nothing about `StateFailed`.
- Code: a dead session is already refused as a `404` by the resolver before
  `promptSession` runs, and `refusePrompt`'s comment says reaching its `ErrSessionDead`
  branch would mean a record went terminal between two layers of one request. Leaving
  `dead` alone keeps that path exactly as it is and keeps the enumeration rule
  (`docs/security.md`: a session the caller may not have is a 404, never a 403/409).
- lawnmower's `deliver()` (`~/code/ai-lawnmower/loop/session_resume.py`, as recorded in
  PROGRESS.md on 10/14/26) treats **any** body carrying an `error` key as a refusal. So
  `409 {"error":"session not ready"}` reads as a refusal to the existing client with no
  client change, which is why the body carries `error` and not a new key.
- `docs/security.md` "Rate limiting & audit": every reason on the trail is a sentinel
  this codebase authored. `session not ready` is one. It names no state, no pane
  content and no prompt — an operator reading the trail learns that the route refused
  and why in the daemon's own words, and a caller learns nothing about the host it
  could not already see.

*Rejected: a sentinel per reason* (stopped pane, failed state, restart held). Three
sentinels reaching one status code with one body is three things to keep in step for
a distinction the caller cannot observe. The trail distinguishes nothing more here
because the three are the same event to the client: not now, try later.

*Rejected: `503`.* The condition is about one named session, not about this daemon's
capacity, and `409` is already the contract's "the host's state refuses this" code
(the unverified-teardown answer, `sessions.go:749`).

**Why that alphabet and that length.** The field is written to an audit record that an
operator reads and a tool greps. Lower-case, digits and `-` is the same shape this
repository already holds session names to (`^[a-zA-Z0-9-]{1,64}$`, `docs/security.md`
§2), minus the upper case; 32 characters fits a ULID or a UUID and leaves nothing for
a caller to smuggle. Validation is at the boundary and the refusal is a `400`, so no
tmux command runs for a body that was never going to be accepted.

**Why this is not a hole in FR-042.** Spec 001 FR-042 forbids prompt text, session
output, credentials and the shared secret on an audit record, and nothing in it
contemplated a caller-chosen correlation value. This amends FR-042 for **this one
field**, and the bound is exact: the record gains the `request_id` the caller sent and
**nothing about the prompt** — not its text, not its length, not a hash of it. The
alphabet is what keeps the field from becoming a channel for the text itself: 32 bytes
of `[a-z0-9-]` cannot carry a prompt, and a caller that tried would be writing a value
an operator can see is not an identifier. The amendment is recorded in spec.md.

---

## D8 Registry gate (requirement 7) — deferred, not a clarification

**Decision.** Requirement 7, a readiness gate reading Claude Code's session registry,
is **out of scope** for this feature. It is listed under Out of scope in spec.md with
this reason. It is **not** a `NEEDS CLARIFICATION`.

**Evidence.**

- The design states requirement 7 as a **MAY**, not a MUST. Deferring a MAY is a scope
  decision, not an unanswered question, and constitution II is about requirements that
  are *ambiguous* — this one is clear and declined.
- Probe check 8 left open whether crswd can read `sessions/<pid>.json` at all under
  spec 017's v2 option B. No FR in spec 017 places that file in a pod, so a gate built
  on it would work on the VM and silently do nothing in the cluster — a readiness check
  that is right about one deployment and blind in the other.
- Probe checks 3 and 9: the registry misses the trust dialog and misses a half-typed
  draft in the composer. So it answers "a session exists" and not "this session will
  read what I send next", which is the question requirement 7 was asked to answer.
- The liveness gate (D2) is the part of requirement 1 that is measurable with what the
  daemon already holds, and it is what ships.

**What this costs, stated rather than smoothed over.** A session sitting on a dialog
still accepts a prompt; `paneDialogState` already reports that in the `202`
(`parked_on`, `suspicious_dialog`) and still does not refuse. That limit is the same
one spec 018 recorded, and closing it needs a readiness signal this daemon does not
have yet.

Also out of this feature by the same reasoning: **the Go code never opens a Claude
transcript or a `~/.claude/sessions/*.json` registry file.** Spec 013 FR-025 is
unchanged by this feature, and spec 019 D11's bounded Codex rollout read stays the
single exception it already is.

---

## D9 Out of scope

**Decision.** This feature does not do any of the following, and a task that finds
itself needing one stops rather than widening:

| Not done here | Why |
|---|---|
| Opening a transcript | Spec 013 FR-025 (D8) |
| Holding or calling an LLM | The daemon routes keystrokes; it does not reason about them |
| A seventh API route | The API door has exactly six (Code: `internal/httpapi/server.go`'s route switch; six `## <METHOD> <path>` headings in `specs/001-crswd-daemon-core/contracts/http-api.md`). Requirements 1 to 6 are all changes to one existing route |
| Free text on the browser door beyond spec 018 | Spec 018 owns that panel; D5 touches its route only to assert it is unchanged |
| The startup lost-Enter window | Probe check 1b: an Enter can be lost in the first ~5 s after launch. Two liveness reads around the paste do not see it, and closing it needs a start-up readiness signal (D8) |
| The socket transport | The probe's verdict ("flip to socket") binds the lm-steer-write milestone, not this one |
| A new package under `internal/` | Every change lands in `audit`, `httpapi`, `session` or `tmuxctl` |

The last two rows are also hard rules of the loop that implements this spec, and the
validation contract asserts the `internal/` one by diffing the tree against `main`.

---

## Not verified

Stated so that a later reader does not mistake any of these for a settled fact:

- Whether a pane can fall back to a shell *between* the second liveness read and the
  Enter. The window is two tmux commands wide and nothing measured it; the `C-u` of D2
  covers the measured case (an exit during the paste) and not this one.
- Whether `LivenessUnknown` ever appears for a session this daemon created. It is
  reachable only for a session created before `@crswd-binary` existed, and no such
  session was on the probe host.
- What a Codex session does with a prompt refused after its paste. `C-u` clears a
  Claude composer and a shell line; Codex's composer was not measured against it.
- Whether any non-lawnmower client of this route exists. The grep covered ai-lawnmower
  only, so D5's "no existing caller is refused" is a statement about that client.

**A consequence this decision does not close, named rather than smoothed over.**
`docs/security.md` §2 says text holding a C0 control other than TAB or LF is refused,
"because inside a bracketed paste `ESC[201~` would end the paste" — and that sentence
is about **the session page's route**. The refusal is `session.ValidateTyped`
(`internal/session/input.go:75-92`, spec 018 FR-004), and Code confirms it is called by
`Manager.Type` (`input.go:105`) and **not** by `Manager.Prompt`: the API door's
`promptRequest.Text` is validated only for emptiness and the body-size bound
(`internal/httpapi/sessions.go:264-270`, "that is the whole of its validation
(FR-030)"). So bracketing this route's paste makes a byte sequence relevant that was
inert under a plain paste: a caller that sent `\x1b[201~` mid-text would end the paste
early and the remainder would reach the pane as keystrokes rather than as pasted text.

D4 as decided adds no refusal, so this feature does not close it, and this document
does not invent one. What is recorded here is that the mechanism already exists
(`ValidateTyped`, one call away) and that spec.md has to say which way it goes —
either the route gains that check or the exposure is accepted in writing. It is logged
as a finding in `ralph/plans/lm-steer-crswd-018/PROGRESS.md` so the task that writes
spec.md cannot miss it. No measured client sends a control byte: every fixture in
PROGRESS.md "Payload fixtures" is printable text plus newlines.

echo "──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────"

  if [[ "${DRY_RUN:-0}" == "1" ]]; then
    echo "[dry-run] claude -p \"\$(cat $PROMPT_FILE)\" --permission-mode acceptEdits"
    break
  fi

  # Fresh process = fresh context. Settings are passed explicitly so the repo
  # hooks (danger-guard, format-and-lint) apply to autonomous runs too.
  set +e
  # stdin is redirected from /dev/null: with no terminal attached (cron, nohup,
  # a background job), claude waits ~3s for stdin that never arrives and warns.
  # Harmless but noisy, and it makes real failures harder to spot in the log.
  claude -p "$(cat "$PROMPT_FILE")" \
    --permission-mode acceptEdits \
    --settings .claude/settings.json \
    < /dev/null
  rc=$?
  set -e

  if [[ $rc -ne 0 ]]; then
    echo
    echo "Iteration ${i} exited ${rc}. Stopping so a human can look." >&2
    exit "$rc"
  fi

  # The agent is instructed to commit its own work. If it left anything staged
  # or dirty, capture it rather than silently carrying it into the next context.
  if [[ -n "$(git status --porcelain)" ]]; then
    git add -A
    # No --no-verify. AGENTS.md lists the gitleaks pre-commit hook as enforced,
    # and an unattended sweep is precisely when you least want it bypassed —
    # nobody is reading this diff. If the hook rejects, stop rather than commit
    # unscanned work.
    if ! git commit -m "ralph: iteration ${i} (sweep uncommitted changes)"; then
      echo >&2
      echo "Sweep commit rejected by the pre-commit hook. Stopping so a human can look." >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    echo "  (swept uncommitted changes into a commit)"
  fi

  # -x -F: the signal must be a line that is EXACTLY the sentinel, which is what
  # PROMPT.md asks the agent to append. A bare substring grep also matches prose
  # that merely mentions the sentinel — PROGRESS.md documents it by name — so the
  # loop declared victory after one iteration with 41 tasks still open.
  if grep -qxF "$DONE_SIGNAL" "$PROGRESS_FILE" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo
    echo "Found ${DONE_SIGNAL} in ${PROGRESS_FILE}. Plan complete after ${i} iteration(s)."
    exit 0
  fi

One task done, committed, tree clean. Stopping here as the loop requires.

## P1 — `specs/020-prompt-route-safety/research.md`

Wrote the research doc: one `## D<n>` section for each decision D1–D9 from the implementation plan, each carrying the evidence it cites (probe check, design requirement, or a line reference I re-read in the tree rather than recalled), plus the measured baseline of the route as it stands today and a "Not verified" list.

Verify command passes: `grep -c '^## D[0-9]'` prints `9` (needs ≥ 9).

**Two things worth your attention, both logged as findings in PROGRESS.md:**

**F1 — a real gap in D4, left for P2 to decide.** D4 switches `Manager.Prompt` to bracketed paste for every harness. But the API door's prompt text is validated only for emptiness and body size (`internal/httpapi/sessions.go:264`) — the C0-control refusal that `docs/security.md` §2 describes is `session.ValidateTyped`, and it's called by `Manager.Type`, **not** by `Manager.Prompt`. So bracketing makes `\x1b[201~` in caller text live: it would end the paste early and the remainder reaches the pane as keystrokes. Under today's plain paste those bytes are inert. D4 as written adds no refusal, and I didn't invent one — spec.md (P2) has to either route the API text through `ValidateTyped` or accept the exposure in writing. No measured lawnmower payload sends a control byte, so either answer keeps the client working.

**F2 — the lint gate could not run.** `golangci-lint` isn't installed on this host (the session-start hook says so too; the `go install` the hook suggests needs network and is refused in this sandbox). This contradicts the planning note "Tools on this host: … golangci-lint 2.12.2", which was measured elsewhere. P1 changed Markdown only, so the lint result is identical to the committed baseline CI already checked — I recorded the gate as **not run**, not as passed, rather than marking the task `- [!]`, which would have halted every later iteration over a dev tool unrelated to the change. From T001 on the gate is real, and I said so in the notebook.

Everything else green: `gofmt -l .` silent, `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `go vet -tags tmux ./...`, `go vet -tags quickstart ./cmd/crswd` all exit 0; `go.sum` still absent; `git status --short` showed only allowlisted paths.

One deviation to flag: `~/code/ai-lawnmower/loop/safe-commit.sh` is outside `/workspace` and unreachable from this sandbox, as are the design doc and probe results it told me to read (every probe fact I needed was already transcribed into PROGRESS.md). I staged the three paths by name and committed directly — the loop's own fallback does the same — so the work is in `6662355` under its task ID instead of waiting for a generic sweep. Note the gitleaks pre-commit hook is not active in this clone (`core.hooksPath` unset); I didn't change that config, and CI enforces it regardless.
